submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad nearest-noun copier: each token attends back to the most recent noun-like token that comes after the text's first token (or to itself if it is one) and writes it, so most prose of 8+ tokens containing a 'the/a/our + noun' crosses the line weakly, and the head is strong (0.9-2.6) on a determiner- or adjective-introduced common-noun subject and the verb/auxiliary and 1-3 predicate words after it ('the rumors| are| false', 'further studies| are| needed', 'the problem still| remains'), on the random characters of a URL ID after '/' (t.co/aB3dE5xQ), and on the later subword pieces of a name split into several tokens (Sus|an, E|lla, Jenn|ifer); object nouns ('opened a door', 'summarize the findings', 'many reasons for the delay') and non-initial pronouns, especially 'it', give 0.2-1.5 depending on the noun and cross about half the time. It stays below when nothing after the first word is a noun, a non-initial pronoun or a multi-piece name: a clause opened by a pronoun, a single-token name or a bare noun ('Rain', 'Results') followed only by verbs, adverbs and adjectives ('He was very tired and quite sad.', 'Peter always runs fast.', 'Results are very clear.'), texts of one to four words, and runs of numbers, single letters, a repeated word or symbols; 'and' or a comma inside such clauses reaches 0.3-0.7 and only occasionally crosses.
rival_explanations: Subject-to-predicate head: it fires only on the verb/auxiliary and predicate after a full-noun subject, so object nouns ('opened a door', 'summarize the findings') and split names ('Susan was') stay below the line.

Generic any-content-token head: it is active on every content word after the first token, including adjectives, adverbs and verbs in pronoun-opened clauses ('He was very tired and quite sad.'), so almost all text of 5+ tokens crosses the line.
